title: Entity Framework Core Tutorials
description: Introduction to EF Core, its version history, development approaches, and database providers.

data.text: **Entity Framework Core** is the new version of Entity Framework after EF 6.x. It is open-source, lightweight, extensible, and a cross-platform version of Entity Framework data access technology.
Entity Framework is an **Object/Relational Mapping (O/RM) framework**. It is an enhancement to ADO.NET that gives developers an automated mechanism for accessing and storing data in the database.
EF Core has evolved significantly since its initial release. Here is the version history:
EF Core supports two development approaches:

items: **Code-First** - EF Core creates database and tables based on your domain classes using migrations
**Database-First** - EF Core creates domain and context classes based on your existing database

data.title: Code-First Preferred
data.text: EF Core mainly targets the code-first approach. Database-First has limited support as there is no visual designer or wizard.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: EF Core is an open-source, cross-platform O/RM framework
Supports Code-First and Database-First development approaches
Multiple database providers available via NuGet
Continues to support EF 6 features with improvements
data.takeaway: Continue to the next lesson to learn how to install EF Core in your project.
